title: Reflected hats have frequency 1 : phi^4, as an integer eigen-relation over Z[phi]
headline: Obsmetrologia.AperiodicOrder.Tiling.Witness.hat_reflection_frequency_witness

requirements.statement: The golden integers Z[phi] are realized as pairs (a, b) standing for a + b*phi with componentwise addition and the multiplication induced by phi^2 = phi + 1, and phi * phi = phi + 1 holds by kernel computation.

The vector v = (1, 5 - 3phi, 6phi - 9, 6 - 3phi) over Z[phi] satisfies v * M = phi^4 * v entrywise for M = hatMetatileMatrix of the HatMetatile module, where phi^4 = 2 + 3phi is the fourth power of phi in Z[phi].

The hats-per-metatile vector (4, 1, 2, 2) and the reflected-hats-per-metatile vector (1, 0, 0, 0) on the alphabet H, T, P, F are stated as integer weight vectors from the monotile paper's metatile composition (an H holds four hats, one of them reflected).

Weighing v by hats per metatile gives 3 + 3phi = 3phi^2, weighing it by reflected hats gives 1, and the unreflected weight (total minus reflected) equals phi^4 times the reflected weight: the ratio phi^4 : 1 as an exact identity in Z[phi].
One headline theorem bundles the golden equation, the left eigen-relation, and the frequency identity.

prohibitions.statement: The module imports only Obsmetrologia core modules, states no RReal, and claims neither uniqueness nor positivity of the eigenvector: Z[phi] carries no order in core, so that v is THE frequency vector (Perron-Frobenius) is left to the frontier node seated beside the headline.
The module does not claim the hat aperiodic and does not transcribe metatile geometry; its scope section says so.

openQuestions.question: Z[phi] as pairs is a primitive the metallic tower (StepN.MetallicMean, StepN.GoldenFieldBridge) should own once a second consumer appears; which StepN module seats it, and does phi^n = F(n-1) + F(n) phi land there against metallicNum 1?
Positivity of 5 - 3phi, 6phi - 9, 6 - 3phi needs an order on Z[phi] (a sign law through the conjugate norm) or the RReal phi of GoldenFieldBridge; which route keeps the frontier node in core?

references: D. Smith, J. S. Myers, C. S. Kaplan, C. Goodman-Strauss, An aperiodic monotile, Combinatorial Theory 4(1) (2024) #6, arXiv:2303.10798, section 2
M. Baake, F. Gaehler, L. Sadun, Dynamics and topology of the Hat family of tilings, arXiv:2305.05639, section 2 eq. (11) and Theorem 4
D. Smith, J. S. Myers, C. S. Kaplan, C. Goodman-Strauss, An aperiodic monotile, section 2: an H metatile holds four hats, one reflected; T one; P and F two each

blueprint.label: thm:hat-reflection-frequency
blueprint.title: Reflected hats have frequency $1:\varphi^4$ as an integer eigen-relation over $\mathbb{Z}[\varphi]$
blueprint.statement: In the golden integers $\mathbb{Z}[\varphi]$ ($\varphi^2=\varphi+1$, elements $a+b\varphi$ as integer pairs) the vector $v=(1,\,5-3\varphi,\,6\varphi-9,\,6-3\varphi)$ is a left eigenvector of the hat metatile matrix $M$ for the eigenvalue $\varphi^4=2+3\varphi$: $vM=\varphi^4 v$ entrywise. Weighted by hats per metatile $(4,1,2,2)$ it gives $3+3\varphi=3\varphi^2$; weighted by reflected hats per metatile $(1,0,0,0)$ it gives $1$; so unreflected $:$ reflected $=\varphi^4:1$ as an exact identity, with no real number and no Perron eigenvector. Every claim is a kernel \texttt{decide} over $\mathrm{Fin}\ 4$ and integer pairs.

frontier.label: thm:hat-perron-frequency
frontier.title: The golden left eigenvector is the hat's frequency vector
frontier.statement: \emph{Open frontier.} $v$ is the unique positive left Perron eigenvector of the primitive matrix $M$ up to scale, so its normalization is the metatile frequency vector of every hat tiling and $1:\varphi^4$ is a frequency. The target is positivity of $5-3\varphi$, $6\varphi-9$, $6-3\varphi$ through an order on $\mathbb{Z}[\varphi]$ (a sign law by the conjugate norm) or through the real $\varphi$ of the golden field bridge, and Perron--Frobenius uniqueness for primitive integer matrices in core.
